title: Windows 11 is quietly installing OneDrive Photos, and it wants to scan your photos for faces if you allow it
excerpt: Microsoft's OneDrive Photos appears to be yet another photo editor and viewer for Windows 11 that nobody asked for.
content_html:
The year is 2026, and I’m still amazed when I find a new entry in my Start menu’s All apps list for an app I don’t remember installing. This time, it’s Microsoft again, and the product is OneDrive Photos, which appears to be yet another photo viewer and editor for Windows 11 that nobody asked to have installed automatically.

While searching for Microsoft Photos, a new app called “OneDrive Photos” showed up in my results out of nowhere. It appears to have arrived either via Windows Update or an update for the OneDrive sync client on Windows.

For those unaware, Windows already comes with OneDrive pre-installed, and it syncs your personal files to the cloud.

Right now, you can manage OneDrive files directly in File Explorer and control sync from the system tray on the taskbar. It looks like the nagging during Windows setup to use OneDrive, along with the backup feature being turned on by default, wasn’t enough, as Microsoft is now adding “OneDrive Photos.”

If Windows has already installed OneDrive Photos on your PC, you can find its entry in the Start menu or Windows Search, whether you’ve signed in to a Microsoft account or not.

In my case, I have the OneDrive sync app installed because it was bundled with Windows, but I haven’t signed in with a Microsoft or work account. I don’t use it. Yet OneDrive Photos still appeared.

Testing the new OneDrive Photos app for Windows 11

In our tests, Windows Latest noticed that the new “OneDrive Photos” app is part of the existing OneDrive installation and runs through “C:\Program Files\Microsoft OneDrive\OneDrive.App.exe.” I also noticed that it’s based on WebView2, so it’s not a native app.

For comparison, the primary OneDrive sync client is “C:\Program Files\Microsoft OneDrive\OneDrive.exe.” So these are two distinct executables, but they’re weirdly named.

OneDrive Photos automatically scans your system storage for photos

OneDrive Photos doesn’t need a Microsoft account to work, as it can also detect your local files. At one point, I started to wonder whether it’ll eventually replace the Microsoft Photos app because it immediately started acting like a second Photos app on my PC.

The app itself isn’t terrible, but that’s not the point. The problem is that Microsoft added another photo viewer without asking, and you can’t remove it separately from OneDrive.

Although OneDrive Photos is a web app and appears to load OneDrive.com’s new design, it performs reasonably well. The interface tries to mimic Windows 11’s acrylic effect and includes dedicated sections for Moments, Gallery, People, Albums, Favorites, and This PC. These are the same sections you’d find on the OneDrive web app, with “This PC” being the exception.

When you open Gallery without signing in to a Microsoft account, the app automatically displays your local images. You can switch between River and Square layouts, choose Roomy or Compact density, and adjust the thumbnail size.

When you open an image, you can edit, share, favorite, copy, delete, print, open it in File Explorer, or set it as your lock screen or desktop background. Again, all of that might sound familiar because it overlaps heavily with the Microsoft Photos app.

Once you sign in, the app becomes a full OneDrive gallery, and you get access to AI-powered cloud search.

For example, you can enter a vague search query, and OneDrive’s AI will try to find the most appropriate image or file. In the case of photos, it can use OCR to read visible text and locate relevant results.

OneDrive Photos app can scan your faces

There’s also a People section that groups similar faces in your photos. Microsoft asks for permission before turning it on and explicitly warns that facial data could be considered biometric data in some regions.

The company says only you can see the grouped faces, that the data isn’t shared with third parties, and that you can delete it by disabling the feature.

OneDrive Photos is clearly more than a simple extension of the OneDrive sync client. It’s a second photo viewer with many of the same features already available in Microsoft Photos.

However, the issue isn’t that OneDrive Photos is unusable. In fact, it’s a decent app in terms of performance and overall UX. The problem is that Microsoft quietly installed another app, gave it access to local photo folders, and tied it to OneDrive so you can’t remove one without removing the other.

If you want to block the OneDrive sync client from installing OneDrive Photos, you’ll need to remove OneDrive entirely from Settings > Installed apps.

今年是 2026 年，当我在“开始”菜单的“所有应用程序”列表中发现一个我不记得安装过的应用程序的新条目时，我仍然感到惊讶。 这一次，又是微软，产品是 OneDrive Photos，它似乎是又一个 Windows 11 的照片查看器和编辑器，没有人要求自动安装。

对于那些不知道的人来说，Windows 已经预装了 OneDrive，它将您的个人文件同步到云端。

如果 Windows 已在你的电脑上安装了 OneDrive Photos，则无论你是否登录到 Microsoft 帐户，都可以在“开始”菜单或 Windows 搜索中找到它的条目。

就我而言，我安装了 OneDrive 同步应用程序，因为它与 Windows 捆绑在一起，但我尚未使用 Microsoft 或工作帐户登录。 我不使用它。 但 OneDrive 照片仍然出现。

在我们的测试中，Windows Latest 注意到新的“OneDrive Photos”应用程序是现有 OneDrive 安装的一部分，并通过“C:\Program Files\Microsoft OneDrive\OneDrive.App.exe”运行。 我还注意到它基于 WebView2，因此它不是本机应用程序。

为了进行比较，主要的 OneDrive 同步客户端是“C:\Program Files\Microsoft OneDrive\OneDrive.exe”。 所以这是两个不同的可执行文件，但它们的名字很奇怪。

OneDrive 照片会自动扫描您的系统存储中的照片

OneDrive Photos 不需要 Microsoft 帐户即可运行，因为它还可以检测您的本地文件。 有一次，我开始怀疑它是否最终会取代微软照片应用程序，因为它立即开始像我电脑上的第二个照片应用程序一样运行。

该应用程序本身并不糟糕，但这不是重点。 问题是微软在没有询问的情况下添加了另一个照片查看器，并且你无法将其从 OneDrive 中单独删除。

尽管 OneDrive Photos 是一款 Web 应用程序，并且似乎加载了 OneDrive.com 的新设计，但它的性能相当不错。 该界面试图模仿 Windows 11 的亚克力效果，并包括“时刻”、“图库”、“人物”、“相册”、“收藏夹”和“这台电脑”的专用部分。 这些部分与您在 OneDrive Web 应用程序中找到的部分相同，但“此电脑”除外。

当您在未登录 Microsoft 帐户的情况下打开图库时，应用程序会自动显示您的本地图像。 您可以在河流和方形布局之间切换，选择宽敞或紧凑密度，并调整缩略图大小。

打开图像时，您可以编辑、共享、收藏、复制、删除、打印、在文件资源管理器中打开它，或将其设置为锁屏或桌面背景。 同样，所有这些听起来可能很熟悉，因为它与 Microsoft 照片应用程序严重重叠。

登录后，该应用程序将成为完整的 OneDrive 库，并且您可以访问人工智能驱动的云搜索。

例如，您可以输入模糊的搜索查询，OneDrive 的 AI 会尝试找到最合适的图像或文件。 对于照片，它可以使用 OCR 读取可见文本并找到相关结果。

OneDrive 照片应用程序可以扫描您的脸部

还有一个人物部分，可以将照片中相似的面孔分组。 微软在打开它之前需要获得许可，并明确警告面部数据在某些地区可能被视为生物识别数据。

该公司表示，只有你可以看到分组的面孔，数据不会与第三方共享，并且你可以通过禁用该功能来删除它。

OneDrive Photos 显然不仅仅是 OneDrive 同步客户端的简单扩展。 它是第二个照片查看器，具有 Microsoft Photos 中已有的许多相同功能。

然而，问题并不在于 OneDrive Photos 无法使用。 事实上，就性能和整体用户体验而言，它是一个不错的应用程序。 问题在于，微软悄悄安装了另一个应用程序，允许其访问本地照片文件夹，并将其绑定到 OneDrive，这样你就无法在不删除另一个应用程序的情况下删除一个应用程序。

如果要阻止 OneDrive 同步客户端安装 OneDrive 照片，则需要从“设置”>“已安装的应用程序”中完全删除 OneDrive。
